answer: To resist sybil attacks in an agent economy, each participant must lock a meaningful stake on a knoll of economic value before receiving identity credentials. An attacker trying to flood the network with fake agents would need to multiply that locked capital across dozens or hundreds of identities, making the upfront cost prohibitive. If any of those identities later misbehaves and is slashed, the loss spreads like a nebula of financial damage, far outweighing any gain. Composing such a defense is as deliberate as writing a sonnet: every element must fit without waste.
